subject: Physics
question: A beaker containing 0.200 kg of water is heated from 20 °C to 40 °C. Calculate the energy supplied (c = 4.18 kJ kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) and describe the change in temperature.
response_text:
ΔT = 40 − 20 = 20 K, so
Q = mcΔT = 0.200 × 4.18 × 20 = 16.72 kJ ≈ 16.7 kJ

The temperature of the water doubled from 20 °C to 40 °C, so the average kinetic energy of its molecules also doubled.

faults.step: The temperature of the water doubled from 20 °C to 40 °C
faults.note: A relative change on the offset Celsius scale is not defined (SI reading, section 12): in kelvin the water goes from 293.15 K to 313.15 K, a rise of 6.8 per cent, so the mean kinetic energy (proportional to T in K) rises by 6.8 per cent, not 100 per cent. [computed: 313.15/293.15 = 1.068, not 2]
